---
title: "Path A · The New Modeler"
subtitle: "Your first defensible population PK analysis in eight weeks"
---

**For:** a junior scientist in industry or a CRO, nought to five years in, who
has a deliverable due and needs to be useful quickly.

**Promise:** you can take raw clinical data to a fitted, evaluated population PK
model and a written report that survives review.

**Ends at:** a written model report, not a converged run. Finishing is a
separate skill from modeling and it is the one employers screen on.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Prerequisite:** [Strand P · Pharmacology from the beginning](../pharmacology.qmd).
Skip it if receptors, ADME and dose–response are already yours. Work it if they
are not — every strand from `S1` onward assumes them.
:::

**Time:** roughly 15–20 hours, including both notebooks per runnable lesson.
Do them in one language. Come back for the second later, or never.

## How to know you have finished

Not "I read the lessons." The bar is:

1. One **complete** analysis — raw data to written conclusion, not a notebook.
2. It is **reproducible** by a stranger from your repository.
3. You can **defend the structure**: why this model, why these covariates, why
   this residual error, and what would have changed your mind.
4. You can **explain it in ten minutes** to someone who does not model.

That is the L2 checklist from [S0-00](../lessons/s0-00-what-is-qp/index.qmd),
and it is what a hiring manager is actually testing for.
